verifier_reason: score=0.0000; output does not meet the accuracy bars

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Function names are clear (yuv420p_to_nv12_process, nv21_to_yuv420p_process) and comments are short ('// R', '// Vectorize 16 chroma pairs'). But business logic uses single-letter names like `s`, `d`, `w`, `h`, and the fixed-point/coefficient logic has almost no documentation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Copy-paste throughout: nv12_to_yuv420p_process and nv21_to_yuv420p_process are near-identical, and every swizzle repeats the same null-check/stride/row loop setup instead of a shared helper. Build cache files (.zig-cache/h/*.txt), zig-out .so and inspect_*.py debug scripts were left in, the scripts outside swscale-impl.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Null planes are checked (`orelse return -1`). But `@intCast(src_stride[0])` into usize would trap on a negative stride, nothing validates sizes at the process boundary, and there are magic numbers (offset 3560 in inspect_scales.py, lane counts).

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: Scalar tails and per-plane strides are present. But `cw = w / 2; ch = h / 2` truncates chroma for odd sizes, where FFmpeg rounds up (-((-w)>>1)), so the last chroma column/row is dropped. The hidden correctness test failed the accuracy bars.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: libswscale_candidate.so builds, and each kernel uses the C-ABI process signature and returns 0 on success. build.zig and the export list are not visible in the diff, so the x86-64-v3 target and exact exports can't be confirmed; the compiled artifact is committed under zig-out.
